title: Working on an early draft
author: ProbablyNotBrazilian
selftext:
Hello, my friends!

For a few years now, I’ve been thinking about a plot I’d like to develop into a story, and I think I finally have something solid to work with.

I’d love to hear about the workflows you’ve developed—what works, what doesn’t, any tips you might have, and the best tools you’ve used.

I’m currently considering creating a 2D or 2.5D pixel-art game using the Godot engine, with some assistance from AI.

My initial plan is to build a prototype and later replace the AI-generated art with assets found online or work created by potential collaborators.

But after seeing some projects around here, I’m no longer sure about the whole question of art.

Perhaps just leave the music and the script-writing free from AI.

Right now, I’ve set up a project within ChatGPT, using it as a sort of journal to organize everything I want to implement—from the story and characters to game mechanics, and so on.

I’d really appreciate your input, if you’re willing to share!

Thanks in advance!

comments.author: ProbablyNotBrazilian
comments.body:
First of all, thanks for getting back to me!

You’re definitely much further along than I am—that’s for sure!

I have a degree in cinema, and long before that, I felt my story would work best as a series—but then I realized its true potential lay in being transformed into an interactive RPG.

It’s only this year that I’ve actually started organizing these ideas, using a sort of "diary" format in ChatGPT (as I mentioned above).

I’m planning on a cast of 16–22 NPCs. I’m still putting their profiles together; so far, I’ve got 4 ready to go.

Like you, I’ve been using AI a lot as a writing partner—getting input on elements I plan to weave into the overarching plot or individual character arcs.

There are a few core mechanics I’m trying to figure out how to implement. Are you familiar with \*Danganronpa\*? It’s a visual novel where, at the end of each chapter, the player has to identify a killer based on clues gathered throughout that chapter.

You do this by engaging in debates with all the characters to uncover the culprit.

I’m trying to come up with a way to incorporate similar debates into my own game—but without the rigid, strictly scripted nature of a visual novel.

I’m also looking for a way to vary the participants in these debates, so it’s not always the same characters involved in every playthrough.

Thanks for all the tips on using AI! I’ll be sure to steer clear of the ones you mentioned having a bad experience with.

I don’t have many friends who are genuinely interested in this kind of creative work—writing scripts or developing games. Most of them are pretty skeptical whenever I talk about my aspirations to create something like this.

I will definitely look for this community's Discord.

But thanks again for the feedback! It’s been really valuable to me!
